title: Case Report: Refractory childhood-onset takayasu arteritis with digital clubbing and extensive supra-aortic and lower-limb arterial disease.
authors: Fawzy M Abunejma; Leen M Jabari; Marah Nouredeen Hamad; Tamer O Tamimi; Omair Bseiso; Hisham Aziz Dweik; Raed M A Isayed; Hanan Qunibi; Waleed Alzaro; Wasef Alhroub
abstract: Childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis is rare, and its early picture is often too vague to point at a large-vessel vasculitis. We report a 12-year-old girl who presented with 13 days of recurrent severe retrosternal chest pain and diffuse colicky abdominal pain, on a background of six months of exertional fatigue and painful swelling of the right fingertips, without fever, weight loss or night sweats. Examination showed bilateral digital clubbing, a right arm blood pressure below the 5th percentile with left arm and lower limb readings between the 50th and 90th percentiles, an absent right radial pulse, and weak brachial and right posterior tibial pulses. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 110 mm/h and C-reactive protein 82 to 93 mg/L. Computed tomography angiography showed mild concentric mural thickening of the aortic arch with severe stenosis of the right common and internal carotid arteries, near-occlusion of the right subclavian artery, moderate to severe brachiocephalic stenosis, moderate narrowing of the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, and moderate stenosis of the right common and superficial femoral arteries. The abdominal aorta and its visceral branches were spared. She met the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES (Ankara 2008) classification criteria for childhood Takayasu arteritis, and the arterial distribution corresponds to Numano type IIa, together with peripheral lower-limb involvement that the Numano scheme does not cover. Disease progressed on intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, methotrexate, aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin, culminating in an 80% stenosis of the right common femoral artery. Adalimumab was started and later replaced by tocilizumab, after which the femoral peri-arterial inflammatory changes resolved on imaging and acute-phase reactants normalized. Blood pressure asymmetry, pulse deficits and the established stenoses persisted. This case suggests that normal inflammatory markers in childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis can coexist with fixed arterial damage, and that judgements about disease activity are better based on clinical findings and serial imaging together than on acute-phase reactants alone.

title: Sex differences in clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a real-world cohort.
authors: Miriam Estévez Táboas; Julio Echarte-Morales; Ernesto José Ruiz Golcher; Carlos Eduardo Sotomayor-Casillas; André González García; David Neuhalfen; Carla Iglesias-Otero; Elena García-Campos Losada; Nazaret Vázquez-Vázquez; David González Fernández; Hugo Prado Prado; Carmen Cuiñas Fariña; Andrés Antelo-Abeijón; Pablo Juan-Salvadores; Rodrigo Estevez-Loureiro; Jose A Baz Alonso; Andres Iñiguez-Romo; Victor Alfonso Jímenez-Díaz
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases in the ageing population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an effective and less invasive therapeutic alternative. Anatomical, pathophysiological, and clinical differences between women and men may influence outcomes following the procedure. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sex and mortality and procedure-related complications after TAVI in a real-world cohort from the Vigo Health Area.
We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including 1,065 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent transfemoral TAVI between 2010 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included bleeding, vascular complications, and new permanent pacemaker implantation. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 365 days; multivariable models used complete-case analysis.
Women were older and had greater frailty and higher surgical risk scores than men. In-hospital and 1-year mortality were similar between sexes. Date-based 30-day mortality was 2.4% in men and 3.7% in women (p = 0.225), and female sex was not independently associated with 30-day mortality after adjustment for age and STS score (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 0.80-3.98; p = 0.154). Female sex was not independently associated with 1-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69-1.66; p = 0.772). Women had more bleeding in unadjusted analyses, but female sex was not significantly associated with any bleeding after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.92-2.81; p = 0.093). Male sex remained associated with higher odds of new permanent pacemaker implantation (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.03-2.17; p = 0.036).
Sex was not independently associated with short- or 1-year mortality after TAVI. Women had a higher unadjusted incidence of bleeding, whereas men had a higher incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation that persisted after adjustment. These findings describe sex-related differences in procedural risk profiles but should be interpreted in the context of the observational design and the long study period.

title: Impact of preprocedural frailty on long-term mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Yang Zhan; Yue Mao; Xiaolan Tang; Rong Li; Mei Li; Daoxin Hua
abstract:
This study aimed to investigate the association between preprocedural frailty and long-term all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception to 15 February 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) with their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
Thirteen cohort studies involving 429,827 patients were included in the systematic review. Of these, 8 studies (4,726 patients) reporting comparable adjusted effect estimates were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. Preprocedural frailty was associated with a higher risk of long-term all-cause mortality after TAVR (HR = 1.85, 95% CI 1.51-2.25; I² = 39.4%). The association was generally consistent across subgroup analyses stratified by follow-up duration and frailty assessment methodology. Five studies that were not amenable to quantitative pooling because of non-comparable effect formats or data structures showed a concordant direction of effect, with some studies demonstrating a graded relationship between increasing frailty burden and mortality risk.
Preprocedural frailty is significantly associated with increased long-term all-cause mortality in older adults undergoing TAVR. These findings support the incorporation of frailty assessment into routine preprocedural geriatric risk stratification and multidisciplinary decision-making.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
authors: Boren Tan; Qifeng Zhu; Qiong Liu; Wenjing Sheng; Kaida Ren; Yuchao Guo; Xinping Lin; Feiyu Wu; Si Cheng; Chongzhou Zheng; Xianbao Liu
abstract:
Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.
Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared.
A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001).
In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.

title: Cardiovascular disease in diabetes mellitus: beyond atherosclerosis and heart failure.
authors: Joanna Y Gong; Spiros Fourlanos; Javed Butler; Peter M Kistler; Christopher M Reid; Dianna J Magliano; Jonathan E Shaw
abstract: The global burden of diabetes mellitus continues to grow, now affecting one in nine adults. In people with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and considerable focus has been placed on reducing the incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure over the past few decades. Due to reductions in the prevalence of some major risk factors, improved control of other risk factors and improved therapeutic agents, mortality attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has declined. Meanwhile, the decline in mortality attributed to heart failure has stalled. However, beyond atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure, many other cardiovascular diseases are responsible for morbidity and mortality. We provide a comprehensive narrative summary of the association between diabetes mellitus and the most common cardiovascular diseases as reported by the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. The evidence indicates that diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for atrial fibrillation, infective endocarditis, hypertensive heart disease, intracerebral haemorrhage and aortic stenosis. We also discuss the available evidence for the effects of incretin hormone mimetics, such as glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, and of sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors for each of these cardiovascular diseases. This Review underscores the multifaceted link between cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus, highlighting that integrated strategies are required to effectively reduce the global burden of both conditions.

title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
authors: Hakan Yalman; Ahmet Atıl Aygün; Mahmut Kaan Temiz; Damla Raimoglou; Murat Çimci
abstract:
Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF.
This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images.
At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity.
In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Maximilian Autherith; Katharina Singer; Laurenz Hauptmann; Christoph Torrefranca; Charlotte Jantsch; Sophia Koschatko; Eva-Maria Röglsperger; Kseniya Halavina; Gregor Heitzinger; Varius Dannenberg; Raghuram Palaparti; Severin Längle; Stéphane Mahr; Caglayan Demirel; Iuliana Coti; Daniel Zimpfer; Christian Hengstenberg; Christian Nitsche; Philipp E Bartko
abstract:
In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.
To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.
DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.
Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.
The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.
Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).
In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.

title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
authors: André Lobo; José Cavadas; Marta Catarina Almeida; Mariana Brandão; Rafael Teixeira; Carolina Castro; Nuno Dias Ferreira; Pedro Braga; Francisco Sampaio; Ricardo Fontes-Carvalho
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

title: Emergent Re-Do Open Aortic Valvular Repair and Foreign Body Retrieval During TAVR: A Case Report.
authors: Ryan Dougherty; Thida Ong; Michael Morgan; Eric Chiang; Aariya Srinivasan; Sabry Ayad
abstract: A 73-year-old man presented for a transcatheter aortic valve replacement after prosthetic aortic valve dysfunction. During the case, the transvenous pacer lost capture, causing the new prosthetic valve to embolize to the ascending aorta. This case details the intraoperative management throughout the valve deployment, attempted retrieval, and subsequent emergent redo open aortic valve repair with foreign body removal. Complications and considerations of a redo open chest, vasoplegia, cardiopulmonary bypass, aortic dissection, right ventricular failure, heart block, and prosthetic valve embolization are discussed.

title: Immune-driven remodeling in calcific aortic valve disease: mechanisms and immunotherapeutic opportunities.
authors: Xi Zhang; Yi Si; Ling Liao; Yuxiang Wu
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent degenerative valvular disorder in the aging population, for which no pharmacological therapy has proven effective in halting or reversing disease progression. Over the past decade, CAVD has been increasingly recognized not as a passive degenerative process of calcium deposition, but as an active, inflammation-driven disease characterized by osteogenic remodeling. This process is initiated and sustained by endothelial injury, lipid retention, immune cell infiltration, and phenotypic transition of valvular interstitial cells. Growing evidence indicates that innate and adaptive immune responses may contribute to disease amplification. Innate immune cells propagate local inflammatory signaling through inflammasome activation, extracellular vesicle communication, protease release, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, while adaptive immune cells further shape disease progression by sustaining cytokine networks that promote fibrosis and osteogenic reprogramming within the valvular microenvironment. Based on these mechanistic insights, this review further discusses emerging translational strategies aimed at targeting key pathogenic processes in CAVD, including modulation of inflammatory signaling, restoration of adaptive immune homeostasis, regulation of extracellular matrix remodeling and antifibrotic pathways, inhibition of VIC osteogenic differentiation, as well as development of patient stratification and local drug delivery approaches. Collectively, these strategies may provide a conceptual framework for earlier, non-surgical interventions for CAVD.

title: Remnant-cholesterol-inflammatory-index as a novel predictor of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis.
authors: Annamaria Mazzone; Melania Gaggini; Ilenia Foffa; Serena Del Turco; Fabrizio Minichilli; Sergio Berti; Cristina Vassalle
abstract:
Inflammaging activates a vicious cycle common to the progression of structural cardiovascular alterations, cardiometabolic diseases as well as degenerative aortic stenosis (AoS). The remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) is a new recently proposed biomarker that combines remnant cholesterol and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, resembling inflammaging. However, the role of RCII in terms of cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular mortality in AoS elderly patients has not been evaluated still now.
to assess the association between RCII and cardiovascular risk factors and mortality in AoS elderly patients.
RCII levels correlated with systemic inflammation biomarkers (closer correlation with interleukin-6), glucose, creatinine, vascular endothelial growth factor and frailty in AoS patients. Inverse correlations were observed with albumin (typically reduced in inflammatory states) and with HDL concentration. The Kaplan-Meier survival estimates showed significantly worse survival in patients with elevated RCII levels (p<0.01) (mean follow-up 19 ± 4 months). In an exploratory multivariable Cox analysis, higher RCII was associated with cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.5, 95% CI: 1.0-12.0).
RCII is associated with cardiometabolic risk and adverse prognosis in elderly patients with AoS, providing an additional perspective on the prognostic implications of the coexistence of lipid abnormalities and low-grade inflammation in this population. However, the limited number of cardiovascular deaths warrants cautious interpretation of this estimate. Moreover, external validation, standardized thresholds, serial measurements, and comparison with established risk models are needed before RCII clinical implementation.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authors: Ahmed Elmorsy Mohamed; Mustafa Abomohsen; Muhammad Haisum Maqsood; Abdul Hakim Almakadma; Zeyad Kholeif; Ahmed Farid Gadelmawla; Rafael Harari; Susheel K Kodali; Islam Y Elgendy; Sripal Bangalore
abstract:
Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.
We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.
Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.
Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

title: Covered-Stent Migration During Same-Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR.
authors: Georgios E Papadopoulos; Ilias Ninios; Vlasis Ninios
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered-stent implantation can restore large-bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon-assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87-year-old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic-isthmus stenosis with a peak-to-peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same-session covered-stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29-mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18-mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic-valve predilation with a 23-mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re-expansion of the stent, a 23-mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic-isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon-assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation.
authors: J Hunter Mehaffey; Stanley B Wolfe; Raymond J Strobel; J W Awori Hayanga; Christopher E Mascio; Leora T Yarboro; Ramesh Daggubati; Bradley S Price; Vinay Badhwar
abstract:
Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population.
Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization.
The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference <0.10). Mean age was 60 years, and many were of low surgical risk <4% (SAVR 69.5% vs TAVI 49.7%). In-hospital mortality (0.41% vs 0.31%; odds ratio, 0.61; p<0.001) and periprocedural stroke (0.31% vs 0.28%; odds ratio, 0.67; p<0.001) favored TAVI. At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR.
For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
authors: Philippe Généreux; Raj R Makkar; Philippe Pibarot; Jeroen J Bax; Brian R Lindman; Kamran Muhammad; J Bradley Oldemeyer; Mark Pirwitz; Colin M Barker; Vinod H Thourani; Pradeep K Yadav; Roberto Rodriguez; Justin Strote; Rahul Sakhuja; Ramzi Khalil; Rahul Sharma; Adnan Chhatriwalla; Jacob M Mishell; Biswajit Kar; Sameer Gafoor; Joseph Walsh; Daniel Spoon; Andrew Frutkin; Andrei Pop; Nicolas M Van Mieghem; Ruby Satpathy; Kenji Ando; Joseph Montarello; John Webb; Sreekanth Vemulapalli; David J Cohen; Aakriti Gupta; Brandon Park; Heather Prince; Philipp Blanke; Michael Mack; Martin B Leon; PROGRESS Trial Investigators
journal: The New England journal of medicine
abstract:
For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome (LEMD2 p.Ser479Phe).
authors: Tacianne R B Delamain; Giseli Casarini; José H H Delamain; Cecilia Boya; Edileide B Correia; Paul Salvador; Dimytri Siqueira; Dorival Della Togna; Fausto Feres; Kleber G Franchini
abstract:
Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome results from the recurrent heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Four cases have been reported, with cardiac involvement absent or only qualitatively described.
A 30-year-old man with short stature, skeletal fragility, and facial dysmorphism presented with syncope from high-grade atrioventricular block. Echocardiography showed premature severe calcific aortic stenosis and mild mitral stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed preserved biventricular function with no late gadolinium enhancement; computed tomography confirmed valvular calcification but no coronary calcium. Chagas serology was negative. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the p.Ser479Phe variant. He received a permanent pacemaker and, 6 months later, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Evaluation also revealed overt type 2 diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and nephropathy: the most advanced metabolic phenotype reported.
This case shows that the p.Ser479Phe variant can cause advanced, intervention-requiring cardiovascular disease (objectively quantified and, to our knowledge, the first in vivo characterization by cardiac magnetic resonance). These findings support routine cardiac and metabolic surveillance in LEMD2-associated progeroid syndromes.

title: Recognizing Arterial Tortuosity Syndrome in Adulthood: A Case Unveiled by Stress Echocardiography.
authors: Parsa Asachi; Aditya R Gandhi; Dan Halpern; Alan F Vainrib; Muhamed Sarić
abstract:
Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder characterized by arterial elongation, tortuosity, and stenosis.
A 31-year-old woman with childhood peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis was referred for preconception counseling. Examination revealed a high-arched palate, narrow facies, dolichostenomelia, and joint hypermobility. Stress echocardiography demonstrated exercise-induced right ventricular systolic hypertension and incidental carotid tortuosity. Computed tomography angiography revealed tortuosity of the aortic arch, celiac trunk, and pulmonary artery branches. Genetic testing confirmed ATS. Pulmonary artery balloon angioplasty and stenting were performed. She was initiated on metoprolol and referred to maternal-fetal medicine.
ATS in adulthood may be identified following incidental findings of arterial tortuosity on imaging. ATS should be considered in patients with these findings and syndromic connective tissue features.
Imaging is crucial in diagnosing ATS. Echocardiographic findings of right ventricular systolic hypertension and arterial tortuosity should prompt consideration of ATS in the right clinical setting.

title: Totally endoscopic mitral valve replacement: reasons for non-feasibility of repair and 5-year outcomes.
authors: Friedrich Sobik; Jonas Pausch; Xiaoqin Hua; Martin Beyer; Evelina Macius; Oliver Bhadra; Yousuf Alassar; Benjamin Kloth; Lenard Conradi; Hermann Reichenspurner; Simon Pecha; Evaldas Girdauskas; Andreas Schaefer
abstract:
Totally endoscopic mitral valve (MV) surgery is an established therapy for mitral regurgitation (MR) with high repair rates at experienced centers. In certain scenarios, however, repair is not feasible, necessitating chordal-sparing MV replacement. This study investigates the reasons for totally endoscopic MV replacement and reports 5-year outcomes.
Between 2012 and 2022, 1,037 consecutive patients underwent totally endoscopic MV surgery. Of those, 75 patients (7.2%) underwent chordal-sparing MV replacement. Preoperative characteristics, periprocedural data, and mid-term outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and compared to a 1:1 propensity score-matched repair group.
After matching, baseline characteristics were balanced. Indications for MV replacement included sclerotic leaflets (28.0%), endocarditis (26.7%), MV stenosis (17.3%), failed repair attempt (17.3%), rheumatic disease (12.0%), and residual MR after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (7%). Cross-clamp and bypass times were similar. Re-thoracotomy occurred in 14.7% vs. 6.7%, while permanent pacemaker implantation occurred solely after replacement (16.0%). Low cardiac output rates were comparable (6.7% vs. 5.5%). Transvalvular gradients at discharge were higher after replacement (p < 0.001). No paravalvular leakage was observed. In-hospital mortality was 4% vs. 0%. Five-year survival was 86.7% vs. 94.7%, and reintervention rates were similar (4.0% vs. 6.7%).
Totally endoscopic MV surgery at a high-volume center is infrequently associated with MV replacement. The main reasons included sclerotic leaflet pathology, MV stenosis, and endocarditis. Despite a higher comorbidity burden and residual baseline imbalance after matching, early and mid-term outcomes were acceptable. Totally endoscopic chordal-sparing MV replacement represents a safe and clinically effective treatment option for selected patients.

title: Evaluation of Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison of Ultrafast and Focused Ultrasound in an In-Vitro Pulsatile Flow Phantom.
authors: Eric Buffle; Rahma Ait Ouaret; Henri Leroy; Ge Zhang; Manon Caudoux; Jerome Baranger; Iris Baron; Guillaume Esclozas; Michael Stucki; Clement Papadacci; Emmanuel Messas; Tania Puscas; Nadia Aissaoui; Alexandre Houdouin; Elie Mousseaux; Gilles Soulat; Mathieu Pernot
abstract:
Mitral regurgitation (MR) severity is assessed by measuring the regurgitant volume (RVol) with echocardiography using the proximal iso-velocity surface area (PISA) method. The low temporal resolution of focused ultrasound, the assumption of hemispheric iso-velocity contours, and the use of a single point to assess the velocity are the pitfalls of this method. This study evaluates a novel method using ultrafast ultrasound, and multiple points for velocity assessment without the aforementioned geometrical assumption to provide a more accurate RVol measurement.
A left heart mock system, comprised of an orifice simulating MR, was filled with water mixed with cellulose. RVols from 20 mL to 70 mL with increments of 10 mL, were delivered by a pulsatile pump which was the reference. Data were acquired at 6000 frames/s by a cardiac phased array probe emitting ultrafast diverging waves, connected to an ultrafast scanner as well as a clinical system emitting focused waves. RVols were computed with the surface integral of the velocity through a planar disk at the input of the orifice with ultrafast transmission (u-PD) and PISA method with focused waves (f-PISA). The error of the two methods was compared.
u-PD showed a significant lower error values than f-PISA (18.6 ± 11.5% and 56.5 ± 4.9%, respectively, p < 0.001).
This study demonstrates that ultrafast ultrasound can provide accurate multi-point estimates of RVol in a model of MR by leveraging the complete axial velocity mapping at high temporal resolution. Its complementary role to PISA method will be evaluated in future clinical studies.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral valve regurgitation: insights from a 5-year prospective multicenter registry.
authors: Salvatore Giordano; Sabato Sorrentino; Salvatore De Rosa; Marco De Carlo; Marianna Adamo; Elisa Pezzola; Francesco De Felice; Mauro Pennacchi; Emmanuel Villa; Diego Maffeo; Paolo Ferraro; Alberto Morello; Michele Cimmino; Michele Albanese; Giuseppe Biondi-Zoccai; Arturo Giordano; Nicola Corcione
abstract: Long-term data on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for significant mitral regurgitation (MR) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and functional and echocardiographic findings during follow-up after MitraClip in a long-term subanalysis of the prospective multicenter GIOTTO registry. We included 406 consecutive patients undergoing MitraClip implantation for significant MR from 6 Italian centers contributing long-term follow-up. Baseline, procedural, in-hospital, and long-term follow-up data were compared according to MR etiology. Predictors of all-cause death were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean follow-up was 56.4±27.2 months. The cohort included 257 (63.3%) patients with functional or mixed MR and 149 (36.7%) with degenerative MR, who were older, more often female, and had smaller ventricles and higher LVEF, whereas functional or mixed MR patients had greater ischemic burden, conduction disease, prior revascularization, pacemaker implantation, and ventricular remodeling. During the overall observation period, crude all-cause death occurred in 161 patients (39.7%) and MVARC-style cardiovascular death in 98 (24.1%), without significant differences between groups. Mitral surgery, repeat TEER, endocarditis, and stroke occurred in 2.2%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 3.5%, respectively. Among patients with available follow-up assessment, 77.5% were in NYHA class I/II. At the actual 5-year landmark echocardiographic assessment, 82.9% had none or mild MR and 97.1% had no more than moderate MR. Independent mortality predictors were older age, lower body mass index, right bundle branch block, MR etiology, larger LV end-systolic diameter, higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure, and longer index hospitalization (all p <0.05). In conclusion, in this prospective multicenter cohort, TEER with MitraClip in high-risk patients was associated with high procedural success and favorable long-term clinical and echocardiographic findings among patients with available follow-up. Mortality appeared to be associated with patient vulnerability, MR etiology, ventricular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and the early post-procedural course.

title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Patient With EED-Related Overgrowth Syndrome.
authors: Aidin Shahilooy; William T Gibson; Shermineh Heydari; Maryam Kiani; Amir Mohammad Roshanaie; Hamid Reza Moazzeni; Ahmad Reza Salehi Chaleshtori
abstract: Cohen-Gibson syndrome (COGIS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in EED. As the COGIS phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely characterized, additional cases help refine understanding of the condition. We evaluated a 37-year-old man with EED-related COGIS features, including overgrowth and intellectual disability. Genetic workup included karyotyping, FMR1 CGG-repeat expansion testing, whole-exome sequencing, and a familial segregation analysis, which identified the previously reported heterozygous pathogenic variant NM_003797.5:c.772C>T:p.His258Tyr. Clinical findings and medical history were recorded; birth parameters were obtained retrospectively from parental report due to lack of official documentation. Echocardiography revealed mild mitral valve regurgitation, alongside features uncommon in previously reported patients-normal adult weight, a long face, normal head circumference, normally spaced eyes, camptodactyly, no history of cryptorchidism, and a normal gait. Notably, the patient's father carried the same variant with reduced Sanger peak height, suggesting possible mosaicism. This case highlights potential phenotypic variability in COGIS, including the cardiac finding warranting further study, and underscores the implications of suspected paternal mosaicism for genetic counseling. Further quantitative assessment of mosaicism and cardiac evaluation in future studies could help better define the clinical spectrum of COGIS.

title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
authors: Ulrich Schäfer; Alexandre Abizaid; Jeffrey J Popma; Nicolò Azzola Guicciardi; Alex Khairkhahan; Davie Campbell; Alexandra Bakall; Irakli Gogorishvili; Tamaz Shaburishvili; Archil Chukhrukidze; Kari Feldt; Fabio Sandoli de Brito
abstract:
Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation.
This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc).
Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes.
The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%).
PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in a Young Man: A Multisystemic Diagnostic Challenge.
authors: Scott Waring; Joseph W Fletcher; Aaron Jones
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex, phenotypically varied disorder that possesses wide-ranging cardiac involvement. Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is one such cardiac manifestation, which results from the deposition of verrucous, sessile lesions favoring the left-sided heart valves. LSE is typically clinically silent without significant valvular dysfunction. Such patients with LSE, however, are those most susceptible to a more severe clinical phenotype resulting from SLE. Here, we report a unique case of a 22-year-old man initially presenting with unilateral leg swelling found to be secondary to a deep-vein thrombosis. He subsequently developed a constellation of acute symptoms, including embolic strokes, splenic infarction, proteinuric kidney injury, and significant mitral regurgitation, all of which mimicked bacterial endocarditis. His complex, multi-systemic disease course presented diagnostic challenges. We highlight the need in such complex cases for a specialist-led multidisciplinary approach, including cardiologists and rheumatologists, to guide serological and radiological investigations. Early use of echocardiography, in particular 3D transesophageal imaging, was paramount in clinching the diagnosis of LSE as an index presentation of SLE and in the transition from intravenous antibiotics to immunosuppression. Our case underscores the importance of the multidisciplinary team and the role of echocardiography in identifying such patients with LSE in SLE and thereby those most vulnerable to significant end-organ sequelae.

title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Anna Damlin; Andreas Rück; Mesud Mustafic; Rebecka Jandér; Anette Rickenlund; Maria J Eriksson; Nawzad Saleh; David Marlevi
abstract:
The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.
All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.
154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).
Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.
Not applicable.

title: 3D Intracardiac Echocardiography-Guided Mitral M-TEER for a Challenging Medial P3 Flail in Patient With Esophagectomy.
authors: Karl Abou Zeid; Charishma Nallapati; Chloe Kharsa; Karl Aramouni; Selin Haci; Nadeen Faza; Stephen Little; Michael J Reardon; Sachin S Goel; Neal S Kleiman; Joe Aoun
abstract:
Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is the standard imaging modality for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER). When TEE is contraindicated, 3-dimensional intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) may provide an alternative; however, published experience remains limited and has predominantly involved central A2/P2 pathology.
A 69-year-old man with severe degenerative MR from a medial P3 flail and prior esophagectomy underwent M-TEER exclusively under 2D/3D ICE guidance. ICE facilitated transseptal puncture, guide positioning, clip orientation, leaflet grasping, and assessment of residual MR and transmitral gradient. One MitraClip XTW was implanted at A3/P3, reducing MR from severe to mild with a mean gradient of 2 mm Hg. He was discharged the following day without complications.
This case demonstrates that comprehensive ICE guidance can extend M-TEER beyond the commonly reported A2/P2 position to challenging medial anatomy.
Comprehensive 2D and 3D ICE can enable safe and effective M-TEER of challenging A3-P3 pathology when TEE is contraindicated or not feasible.

title: Hemodynamic-Guided Management of Moderate Secondary Mitral Regurgitation and Chronic Heart Failure.
authors: Kyle Roter; JoAnn Lindenfeld; Kashish Goel; Sandip K Zalawadiya
abstract:
Contemporary guidelines recommend mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (mTEER) for patients with heart failure (HF) and moderate-to-severe or severe secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) who remain symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy. The benefits of mTEER in patients with chronic HF and moderate SMR are unclear.
A 65-year-old woman with chronic HF and moderate SMR underwent implantable pulmonary artery pressure sensor placement. Pulmonary artery diastolic pressures remained elevated (>20 mm Hg) despite diuretic escalations, and she was hospitalized for acute HF. She underwent mTEER, resulting in a sustained improvement in pulmonary artery diastolic pressure (≤20 mm Hg), functional class, subjective quality of life, and no further HF hospitalizations. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: The SMR was moderate by echocardiography and would not have met guideline-supported severity criteria for mTEER.
Hemodynamic-guided management may help select patients with HF and moderate SMR who might benefit from mTEER.
Current guidelines do not establish a role for mTEER in patients with HF and moderate SMR who remain symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy. Longitudinal hemodynamic monitoring may support multidisciplinary assessment when symptoms and congestion appear disproportionate to SMR severity by echocardiography.

title: Targeted Transcatheter Mitral Edge-to-Edge Repair for Dynamic Systolic Anterior Motion After Mitral Valve Repair.
authors: Ibrahim Naoum; Juliana Perez Pinzon; Miles Shen; Melissa Todice; Marc Pelletier; Emmanuel Akintoye; Amit N Vora

title: Perioperative Care of Heart Failure, Arrhythmias, and Valvular Heart Disease.
authors: Avital Y O'Glasser; Efrén C Manjarrez
abstract: Frequently, the question of whether or not a patient is stable for surgery boils down to the question, "Does this patient need a preoperative stress test?" However, coronary artery disease and ischemic heart disease are only some of the many cardiac conditions that patients present with preoperatively-and that can negatively impact their intraoperative management and postoperative outcomes. This article will explore the evidence based, patient centered best practices surrounding the perioperative evaluation and management of heart failure, arrhythmias, and valvular heart disease.

title: Development and external validation of a preprocedural prediction model for 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Qi Chen; Thierry Donati; Monika Hebeisen; Florian A Wenzl; Neria E Winkler; Panagiotis Savvoulidis; Chantal Wohlwend; Jonathan Michel; Barbara Stähli; Albert M Kasel; Thomas F Lüscher; Felix C Tanner
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established treatment for severe aortic stenosis but not recommended for patients with a life-expectancy below 1 year. Nevertheless, 1 year mortality after TAVI is around 15% in current reports. Accurate prediction models are thus needed to prevent futile interventions.
Patients undergoing TAVI were prospectively recruited between 2008 and 2021 from a single-centre registry in Zurich, Switzerland and data split into derivation and validation datasets. Four expert cardiologists defined relevant candidate predictors. A prediction model was developed using multiple logistic regression after imputation of missing data. An independent cohort undergoing TAVI from 2008 to 2018 in London, UK served as an external validation dataset. Performance of the prediction model was assessed through internal and external validation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calibration plots were used for discrimination and calibration.
A total of 1702 patients were included from the Swiss cohort. Among these 1278 were used for model development and 424 for validation. 12 predictors were incorporated including age, male sex, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, haemoglobin, creatinine, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, troponin, left ventricular ejection fraction, mean transaortic pressure gradient and severe mitral regurgitation. The prediction model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.72 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.81) in internal validation and showed optimal sensitivity and specificity for 1-year mortality prediction at a probability threshold of 20%, outperforming European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II and Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) score. In the external validation dataset consisting of 851 patients from the UK cohort, the AUC was 0.64 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.70).
The TAVI-specific risk model demonstrated acceptable performance for prediction of 1-year mortality after TAVI across two contemporary real-world cohorts, highlighting its potential for clinical application instead of EuroSCORE II or STS-PROM.

title: Posterior Mitral Leaflet Length and Outcomes After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: From The OCEAN-Mitral Registry.
authors: Sachiyo Ono; Shunsuke Kubo; Mikitaka Fujita; Naoki Nishiura; Kazunori Mushiake; Kohei Osakada; Takeshi Maruo; Mitsuru Abe; Masanori Yamamoto; Atsushi Sugiura; Tetsuro Shimura; Mike Saji; Masahiko Asami; Yusuke Enta; Shinichi Shirai; Masaki Izumo; Shingo Mizuno; Yusuke Watanabe; Yuki Izumi; Makoto Amaki; Kazuhisa Kodama; Hisao Otsuki; Daisuke Hachinohe; Toru Naganuma; Hiroki Bota; Yohei Ohno; Masahiro Yamawaki; Hiroshi Ueno; Gaku Nakazawa; Toshiaki Otsuka; Kentaro Hayashida; OCEAN-Mitral investigators
abstract:
A short posterior mitral leaflet (PML) length is challenging anatomy for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER); however, its prognostic impact remains unclear.
This study evaluated the association between PML length and M-TEER outcomes.
A total of 2,441 patients with functional mitral regurgitation (MR) were stratified by preprocedural PML length: very short (7 mm or less, n = 82), short (>7-10 mm, n = 736), and adequate (>10 mm, n = 1,623) groups. Procedural outcomes, echocardiographic data, and all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization were compared.
Median follow-up was 14.4 months [Q1-Q3: 10.2-27.5]. At discharge, MR grade 1+ or less was comparable among the 3 groups (very short: n = 63/82, 77% vs short: n = 598/736, 81% vs adequate: n = 1,259/1,623, 78%; P = 0.129). At 1 year, MR grade numerically worsened in the very short group (MR grade 1+ or less, n = 31/52, 60%). The rate of achieving both MR grade 1+ or less and transmitral mean pressure gradient <5 mm Hg was similar among groups at discharge, but it was significantly lower in the very short group (n = 14/39, 36%) than in the short (n = 201/306, 66%) and adequate (n = 440/665, 66%) groups (P < 0.001) at 1 year. Although the incidence of the composite outcome was higher in shorter groups (P = 0.018), the PML length was not an independent risk factor in the multivariate analysis.
M-TEER may be feasible in selected patients with shorter PML; however, very short PML might have less favorable echocardiographic durability, warranting anatomical assessment and follow-up. Given the small subgroup and limited follow-up, these findings require cautious interpretation and validation.
OCEAN-Mitral registry (UMIN000023653).

title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
authors: Takashi Nagasaka; Vivek Patel; Kazuki Suruga; Hidemasa Shitan; Yuchao Guo; Ofir Koren; Alon Shechter; Dhairya Patel; Tarun Chakravarty; Aakriti Gupta; Hideki Ishii; Hasan Jilaihawi; Moody Makar; Mamoo Nakamura; Raj R Makkar
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.
We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.
Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.
In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

title: Unilateral pulmonary oedema secondary to acute severe mitral regurgitation mimicking pneumonia: A case report.
authors: Elsayed Khalil; Mohamed Abada; Ahmed Hamada
abstract: Unilateral pulmonary oedema is a rare and frequently under-recognized manifestation of acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema. Its unilateral radiographic appearance often mimics pneumonia, leading to diagnostic delay, and inappropriate initial management. Acute severe mitral regurgitation is among the most important cardiac causes of unilateral pulmonary oedema, particularly when associated with eccentric regurgitant jets directed toward the pulmonary veins.

title: Stuck in the Traffic-Light: Moving Past Color Signals to Real Decisions in Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Therapy Management.
authors: Vratika Agarwal; Firas Zahr
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
abstract: Historically, the complexity of patients being evaluated for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge therapy (M-TEER) has been divided into 3 main categories: green zone: defined as cases where M-TEER is straightforward and not complex, yellow zone: cases with medium complexity where M-TEER is feasible but not entirely straightforward, and red zone: cases where you would not consider M-TEER as the first option and may be swayed toward consideration of other options like transcatheter mitral valve (MV) replacement or surgical management. However, the advancement in preprocedural planning with precise anatomical definition by 3-dimensional imaging modalities has changed how we address complex mitral regurgitation cases. The expansion of available devices for management of MV disease has changed the way we think about undertaking challenging M-TEER procedures. Management in the current era emphasizes meticulous preprocedural assessment of mitral regurgitation pathology, strategic planning for device implantation, judicious device choice, and early consideration of transcatheter MV replacement or other innovative transcatheter devices. This review article provides a comprehensive overview of the available data on M-TEER and outlines treatment strategies for complex cases within the context of contemporary transcatheter technologies.

title: Beyond mortality prediction after mitral TEER: Which risks remain modifiable?
authors: Teruhiko Imamura
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions

title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 concentration in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
authors: Naoki Iwasa; Mamu Shimizu; Tomoko Okamoto; Hiroto Kosuga; Nayu Morikita; Mifumi Kawabe; Munetaka Iwata; Kazuhiro Watanabe; Yui Kobatake; Satoshi Takashima; Naohito Nishii
abstract:
Circulating fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) is primarily a kidney-related biomarker, but also may be influenced by cardiovascular remodeling and hemodynamic load.
Verify whether serum FGF-23 concentration increases with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) severity.
Forty-two client-owned dogs with MMVD without overt kidney disease.
Retrospective cross-sectional study to evaluate serum FGF-23, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine (Cr), and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentrations. Imaging variables included vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), left atrial-to-aortic root ratio (LA/Ao), normalized left-ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN), and diastolic transmitral E-wave velocity (E-vel). Differences among American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine stages were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Correlations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with serum FGF-23 concentration.
Dogs with ACVIM stages C and D had higher serum FGF-23 concentrations than those with stages B1 and B2 (P < .05). Serum FGF-23 concentrations were positively correlated with VLAS (rs = 0.500, P < .01), ANP (rs = 0.455, P < .01), LA/Ao (rs = 0.384, P < .05), E-vel (rs = 0.372, P < .05), and NT-proBNP (rs = 0.366, P < .05). ACVIM stage was significantly associated with serum FGF-23 concentration after adjustment for serum Cr concentration and loop diuretic use.
The potential influence of MMVD should be considered when interpreting increased circulating FGF-23 concentrations in dogs with MMVD.

title: Severe Hypercoagulability With Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis After KRAS Inhibitor Exposure: A Perfect Storm.
authors: Cecilia Villa-Etchegoyen; Raymond B Fohtung; Kwan S Lee; Chadi Ayoub; Reza Arsanjani
abstract:
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a rare malignancy-associated condition causing systemic embolization and valvular dysfunction. Its presentation as new severe mitral regurgitation (MR) may be difficult to recognize.
A 76-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma developed progressive dyspnea after treatment with the KRAS inhibitor daraxonrasib. Echocardiography demonstrated new severe MR with leaflet thickening and broad-based echodensities. His course was complicated by pulmonary embolism, recurrent coronary thrombosis, and persistently negative blood cultures. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed bilateral leaflet involvement with a central coaptation defect. Anticoagulation was changed to low-molecular-weight heparin.
NBTE should be considered in patients with malignancy presenting with new MR and thrombotic events without evidence of infection. The temporal association with KRAS inhibition is noteworthy but does not establish causality.
NBTE may present as subacute MR. Echocardiography and clinical context are essential for timely diagnosis and management.

title: Can the QTc interval and T-wave morphology change intermittently in arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse? First paediatric case experience.
authors: Senem Özgür; Serpil Kaya Çelebi; Selman Kesici; Murat Akkus; Yakup Ergul
abstract:
Mitral valve prolapse is typically considered a benign condition. However, a newly described repolarisation anomaly known as arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is closely associated with repolarisation disturbances and can potentially lead to sudden cardiac death. Arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is characterised by bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, mitral valve regurgitation, T-wave inversions in the inferolateral leads, and complex ventricular ectopy.
In this case, we present the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in a 16-year-old adolescent girl who experienced sudden cardiac arrest during exercise. Her electrocardiograms revealed intermittent QT/QTc prolongation. Interestingly, QT prolongation was always associated with T wave inversion in inferolateral leads. Heterozygous genomic changes were detected in the KCNH2 gene and the 25th exon of the ANK2 gene. These findings support the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in this patient.
Since mitral valve prolapse is a common condition in the society, it is important to determine beforehand which ones are at risk of sudden death. As these boundaries are drawn better, underdiagnosis as well as overdiagnosis will be prevented.

abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.
